Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testIterateDOM()` calls `doTestIterate(DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM)`. This calls the `doTestIterate` method which asserts that iterating with an XPath expression on a JXPathContext created with the DOM model returns specific pointers to elements with prefix "a".

The test and bug report show that when there are multiple prefixes referring to the same namespace URI in the XML document (like 'a' and 'b' both mapped to the same "ns"), `JXPathContext.iteratePointers()` mistakenly returns the first element twice but misses the second element with a different prefix.

The code snippet for `iteratePointers()` in JXPathContext is abstract, so the issue is likely in the underlying iterator implementation that returns elements for the namespace-qualified XPath query.

From the iteration code snippet (`DOMNodeIterator.next()`), the iteration logic walks sibling nodes and filters children nodes. The testChild() method, likely responsible for filtering to the relevant namespace and local name, presumably does not correctly handle multiple prefixes mapping to the same namespace URI. This causes it to return the first matching element twice (perhaps once for each prefix) and skip the second element with a different prefix.

Hence, the root cause of the failure is the iterator in `org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.dom.DOMNodeIterator` that does not correctly distinguish elements by namespace URI regardless of prefix, causing duplicate returns and missing elements during iteration.

The bug report cut-off message also points to this: "This is because in class org.apache.commons.jx" and likely goes on to describe that the iterator uses namespace prefixes instead of URI for filtering.

Suggested fix is to ensure namespace matching during iteration relies on the namespace URI, not the prefix, thus returning all elements in the namespace regardless of prefix and without duplicates.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
